en: Udāna 1.10 Bāhiyasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time Bāhiya Dārucīriya was staying at Suppāraka on the seashore, where he was honored, revered, esteemed, venerated, and respected, and was a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
Then, while Bāhiya Dārucīriya had gone into seclusion and was dwelling in retreat, this reflection arose in his mind:
“Whoever in the world are arahants, or have entered the path to arahantship— I am one among them.
Then a deity who was formerly a blood relative of Bāhiya of the Bark-cloth, compassionate and wishing for his welfare,
knowing with her own mind the reflection in Bāhiya of the Bark-cloth’s mind, approached Bāhiya of the Bark-cloth.
Having approached Bāhiya of the Bark Robe, he said this to him:
“Bāhiya, you are neither an arahant, nor have you entered the path to arahantship.
Furthermore, you do not possess that practice by which you might become an arahant or enter the path to arahantship.”
“Then who, indeed, in this world with its devas are arahants, or have entered the path to arahantship?
“There is, Bāhiya, in the northern regions a city named Sāvatthī.
There the Blessed One currently dwells—he who is an arahant, a perfectly awakened Buddha.”
“For indeed, Bāhiya, the Blessed One is an arahant and teaches the Dhamma for the sake of arahantship.
Then Bāhiya of the Bark Robe, stirred by that deity, departed from Suppāraka at once.
Staying overnight at every place along the way, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī, at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus were walking back and forth in the open air.
Then Bāhiya Dārucīriya approached those bhikkhus; having approached, he said this to them:
"Where, venerable sirs, does the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwell at present?"
“We desire to see that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
“Bāhiya, the Blessed One has entered among the houses for alms.
Then Bāhiya of the Tattered Robe, departing quickly from Jetavana, entered Sāvatthī.

He saw the Blessed One walking for alms in Sāvatthī—inspiring confidence, inspiring faith, with senses calmed, mind at peace, having attained the highest self-mastery and tranquility, tamed, guarded, with senses restrained, a true elephant among men.
Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet and said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma;
let the Sugata teach me the Dhamma, which will lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time.
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Bāhiya of the Bark Robe:
“It is not yet the right time, Bāhiya, for we have entered among the houses for alms.
A second time, Bāhiya of the Tattered Robe said this to the Blessed One:
“But it is difficult to know, Bhante, whether there will be obstacles to the Blessed One’s life or obstacles to my own life.”
“Teach me the Dhamma, Bhante;
teach me the Dhamma, Sugata, which may lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time.
A second time, the Blessed One said this to Bāhiya of the Bark Robe:
“It is not yet the right time, Bāhiya, for we have entered among the houses for alms.
A third time, Bāhiya Dārucīriya said this to the Blessed One:
“But it is difficult to know, Bhante, whether there will be obstacles to the Blessed One’s life or obstacles to my own life.”
“Teach me the Dhamma, Bhante;
teach the Dhamma, Sugata, which may lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time.
“Therefore, Bāhiya, you should train yourself thus:”

‘In the seen there shall be only the seen; in the heard there shall be only the heard; in the sensed there shall be only the sensed; in the cognized there shall be only the cognized. Thus, Bāhiya, should you train yourself.

When, Bāhiya, in the seen there shall be only the seen for you; in the heard there shall be only the heard; in the sensed there shall be only the sensed; in the cognized there shall be only the cognized—
Therefore, Bāhiya, you are not "by that. Since you are not "by that," Bāhiya, you are not "therein."
“Since you, Bāhiya, are not there, therefore, Bāhiya,
you are neither here nor beyond, nor between the two.
This itself is the end of suffering.”
Then, at that very moment, through this brief teaching of the Dhamma by the Blessed One, Bāhiya of the Bark Robe’s mind was liberated from the taints by non-clinging.
Then the Blessed One, having exhorted Bāhiya of the Bark Robe with this brief instruction, departed.
Not long after the Blessed One had left, a cow with a young calf fell upon Bāhiya of the Bark Robe and took his life.

Then the Blessed One, having walked for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from his almsround after his meal, went out from the city together with a number of bhikkhus. He saw that Bāhiya Dārucīriya had passed away;
seeing him, he addressed the bhikkhus:
“Bhikkhus, take up the body of Bāhiya Dārucīriya; place it on a bier, carry it out, and cremate it; then build a stupa for him.”
“Bhikkhus, your fellow practitioner has passed away.
“Yes, Bhante,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
Having placed Bāhiya Dārucīriya’s body upon a bier, they carried it out, cremated it, and erected a stupa for him. Then they approached the Blessed One.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Sitting there, those monks said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, the body of Bāhiya of the Bark Robe has been cremated, and a stupa has been erected for him."
“What is his destination, what is his future state?
“Bhikkhus, Bāhiya of the Bark Robe was wise; he practiced in accordance with the Dhamma and did not trouble me regarding the Dhamma.
Bhikkhus, Bāhiya of the Bark Robe has attained final Nibbāna.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Where water and earth,
fire and wind find no footing;”
There the stars do not shine,
nor does the sun radiate;
there the moon does not gleam.
Darkness does not exist there.
And when one experiences this by oneself,
the sage is a brahmin through his sagehood.
Then, whether with form or formless,
one is liberated from pleasure and pain. Thus ends the tenth [sutta].
"This too is an inspired utterance spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The first chapter, the Bodhi-vagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
Tayo, Bodhi, Huṃhuṅka,
Brāhmaṇa, Kassapa, Aja,
Saṅgāma, and Jaṭila.
"Bāhiya" refers to those ten.
